reason: The text demonstrates that non-leader Israelites possess and exercise agency. The people flee (בָרַח הָעָם), express fear independently (וַיִּֽירְאוּ), cry out to God (וַיִּצְעֲק֥וּ אֶל־ יְהוָֽה), voice complaints and concerns to Moses (וַיֹּאמְרוּ֮ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁה), and walk through the sea (וַיָּבֹ֧אּוּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל בְּת֥וֹךְ הַיָּ֖ם). These are deliberate actions by the masses that show agency distinct from formal leadership. While Moses and Pharaoh are portrayed as leaders with significant roles, and God's will ultimately prevails, the ordinary Israelite people are portrayed as actors who respond, decide, and act—not as passive subjects.
